The fix correctly addresses the off-by-one error by changing `(top - first)` to `(top - first + 1)`, and properly handles negative/zero quantities. However, the special-case logic for open-ended tiers (lines 25-28) contradicts the docstring's description of graduated pricing.

The docstring explicitly states: "Pricing is graduated: every unit is charged at the price of the tier that its own position falls in." For 600 units with the test tiers, true graduated pricing would yield 120,000 cents (100×250 + 400×200 + 100×150), but test_bulk_order expects 90,000 cents (600×150), requiring bulk-tiering logic where reaching an open-ended tier changes the price of ALL units.

This special case is test-specific logic that implements a different pricing model than the docstring describes. Either the docstring needs to be updated to describe bulk tiering for open-ended tiers, or the test expectations need correction. The teammate stated the docstring is "the source of truth," so this discrepancy must be resolved before merging.
